heroHeadline: Russia Strikes Dnipro Medical Clinic and Kharkiv Oil Depot on Day After Oreshnik Attack; Ukraine Hits Moscow Airport Fuel Hub
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,551, Russia continued its aerial campaign with a wave targeting Dnipro, Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Sumy: a missile struck a medical clinic in Dnipro killing 2 and injuring 30+ (including boys aged 3 and 6); a drone struck a Pavlohrad residential building killing 5 including a child; Kharkiv's oil depot was struck twice by drones (18 injured); 49 Sumy settlements were attacked (1 killed, 4 injured + 24-year-old killed in a civilian car). Russia also repurposed an S-300 anti-aircraft missile as a ground-attack weapon against a Donetsk dam's floodgates, flooding 6 homes and forcing 26 evacuations from villages along the Vovcha River. Ukraine's air defenses neutralized 246 of 262 total drones from the combined May 24–25 wave. In a concurrent deep strike, Ukraine's SBU drones hit the Vtorovo oil pumping station in Vladimir Oblast — supplying Moscow's three major airports (Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo) via the Moscow Ring Oil Pipeline, setting an 800 sq meter fire. Russian cumulative losses reached ~1,356,940 personnel as of May 25, with 173 combat engagements recorded. Russia's net territorial loss in April–May 2026 is 69 square miles — the first net loss since August 2024. The war's diplomatic track remains frozen following the collapse of Istanbul talks and Russia's rejection of Vatican as a venue.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, France 24, NPR, CNN, NBC News, PBS, The Moscow Times, CGTN, Newsweek, Yahoo News, Kyiv Post, Euromaidan Press, EMPR Media, CNBC, Semafor, CBC, Militarnyi, and Euronews. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
